close_reason: Landed in 5417494. WrongLength.got and NonHexLowercase.at switched from usize to u32 with saturating u32::try_from(_).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) at the construction site. Eliminates platform-dependent integer width from the public error contract.
description:
crate-jmap-cid-types/src/digest.rs:35-38 declares:

    WrongLength {
        got: usize,
    },

The candidate's byte length is bounded by the maximum length of any &str a caller can possibly pass. Practically, the value is going to be in 0..=128 for any sensible diagnostic — the spec ABNF length is 64, and the only inputs where a much larger length would be informative are pathological (and even then, capping the diagnostic at u32::MAX bytes is more than enough).

Using usize bakes 64-vs-32-bit platform-dependence into the public error type:

  - The Debug-printed representation will differ in layout assumptions between 32-bit and 64-bit targets (relevant only for diagnostic-byte-output tests, but those exist).
  - Error structs that are serialized into logs or transmitted over IPC (jaeger, OTLP) will carry an integer whose maximum-value range depends on the target.
  - Consumers building cross-platform wire diagnostic payloads (e.g. an error report uploaded from a 32-bit ARM client to a 64-bit x86_64 server's aggregator) carry an inconsistency that is invisible until someone tries to deserialize a wide value.

A bounded type — u32 (or even u16) — fixes the contract and matches the actual value range. The cost is a `as u32` or `as u16` cast at the construction site (digest.rs:115), which can saturate or panic on overflow — for a value bounded by usize that came from &str length, this won't actually overflow in practice on any platform with addressable memory under 4 GiB.

This is an api-contract,leakage finding in the workspace's terms: the public surface leaks a platform-dependent implementation detail (Rust's choice of usize for collection lengths) where a fixed-width integer would have been equivalent in semantics and more portable. The same critique applies to NonHexLowercase { at: usize } — both are bounded by the 64-byte input.

Worth fixing in v0.1.0 before consumers code error-deserializer logic against the usize shape.
title: Sha256DigestErrorKind::WrongLength { got: usize } uses platform-dependent type for a bounded value
